order: Add a .gitattributes file that pins line endings to LF for shell, JavaScript, and Markdown files, and mark install.sh executable in the repository. The goal is to stop a checkout on any platform from silently converting install.sh to CRLF, which breaks its POSIX shebang line and makes the installer fail to run on Unix machines. Scope is exactly two changes: the new .gitattributes rules and the executable bit on install.sh — leave install.sh's contents alone; its file mode changes, and no other change is made, so the diff shows zero insertions or deletions inside the script itself. Cover only the file extensions that matter for this installer path (.sh, .js, .md); widening the rule set to every text file in the tree risks rewriting files whose line endings are meaningful elsewhere, so stop there. Keep the fix narrow enough that a reviewer can confirm its effect from the .gitattributes diff alone, start to finish.
claims: Added .gitattributes with LF rules for sh/js/md files and set install.sh's executable bit; no other file content changed. This keeps a checkout on any platform from corrupting the installer's shebang line, since git now normalizes those extensions to LF regardless of the checking-out machine's default line-ending setting. Verified by inspecting the diff: 5 lines added to .gitattributes, install.sh shows 0 insertions and 0 deletions — a mode-only change.
